Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of Ireland. It will be the duo of Saim Ayub and Mohammad Rizwan that will open the innings for Pakistan. Mark Adair will get proceedings underway with the ball here.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 107 needed for Pakistan to end a disappointing campaign with a win and the pitch does now look decent to bat on. Still, given what we have seen in this tournament so far, Ireland aren't out of the contest one bit but will need to pick up early wickets if they are to pull off a remarkable win. Stay tuned as the chase is up next.

Shaheen Afridi is up for a quick chat. He says that he was trying to take wickets from the first ball and was following to stick to his plan to bowl fuller and swing it. Mentions that the ball was seaming and the bowlers did really well to restrict Ireland to this total. Adds that the batters need to be a bit watchful as the new ball is doing tricks and it gets easier to bat on with once the ball gets a bit old and hopes that the batters will get them over the line in this game.

Another rather shoddy display with the bat from Ireland, especially from that faltering top order that has been under fire throughout the competition. The highly experienced likes of Andy Balbirnie and Paul Stirling got out inside the first two overs and then Lorcan Tucker and Harry Tector too couldn't do anything. There was some resistance from the middle order and Gareth Delany was the best of the lot as he scored a quickfire 31 off 19 balls. Mark Adair too played a decent knock before Joshua Little struck a few lusty blows in the death overs but overall, they were well below their best and now have a big job at hand with the ball.

A comprehensive bowling display from Pakistan and they have kept Ireland down to a meager total of 106 for 9 but Pakistan will still feel they have given away 10-15 runs more than they should have in the end. After winning an important toss, Babar Azam opted to bowl first and the two frontline seamers, Shaheen Afridi and Mohammad Amir made great use of the new ball and the early seam-friendly conditions. Shaheen got a couple of wickets in the first over that got Pakistan on their way and Amir followed it up by some really tight bowling. They had the opposition reeling inside the Powerplay after which Haris Rauf came in and did some damage as well. The other bowlers didn't bowl particularly well but then Imad Wasim came in and ran through that lower order by picking up three wickets before there was some resistance by the final batting pair and they failed to bowl Ireland out.
Darts one quicker on off, Joshua Little rolls this to long on for one to close the innings. Ireland manages to score 106 after 20 overs.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Mohammad Amir to Curtis Campher, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another appeal for caught behind but turned down. Pitched up outside off stump and slanting across the right-hander, Curtis Campher looks to drive but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mohammad Amir to Curtis Campher, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: George Dockrell is in at number 6.

OUT! LBW! Finally, Shaheen Afridi does get one decision his way and Pakistan now have their fourth wicket. Very full again and on middle and leg stump, swinging back in a fair bit. Harry Tector looks to get across the stumps and flick it away but misses and gets hit on the boot of the back leg. Shaheen pleads for the LBW and the finger goes up. No review taken by Tector and he walks back after a brief discussion with the non-striker. Oh, dear! The replays show that the ball was pitching outside leg stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shaheen Afridi to Harry Tector, OUT! lbw b Shaheen Afridi.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off stump, tentatively played away towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Shaheen Afridi to Harry Tector, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Full and outside off stump, angling away, Harry Tector looks to play the expansive cover drive but the ball zips past the outside edge and straight to the keeper. Shaheen Afridi feels there is an outside edge but doesn't get much support. No reviews left though and the replays show that indeed there was a faint edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shaheen Afridi to Harry Tector, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off stump, squeezed away on the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Shaheen Afridi to Curtis Campher, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another huge appeal for LBW but it is turned down. That was really full but seemed to be swinging a fair bit as well and Babar Azam has taken the review. Shaheen Afridi pitches this one up very full and right at the toes, Curtis Campher looks to flick it away but misses and gets hit right on the toes. The ball shoots off the toes and goes over the slip cordon into the fence. Nothing on UltraEdge and Ball Tracking shows that it pitched outside leg stump. It will be four leg byes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Shaheen Afridi to Curtis Campher, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length and in the channel around off stump, this one doesn't nip back in either and Curtis Campher plays well inside the line of that one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shaheen Afridi to Curtis Campher, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: TWO WIDES! That just kept on going! A bit fuller but well wide of the off stump and this one keeps angling away after pitching. Mohammad Rizwan springs across but can't get to it and the batters get an extra run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shaheen Afridi to Harry Tector, 2 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that is a risky shot from Curtis Campher. On a hard length on leg stump and shaping back in a long way. Curtis Campher charges down the track and looks to thump it down the ground but is beaten all ends up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mohammad Amir to Curtis Campher, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, that nipped back in sharply! Good length around the top of off stump and angling back in a long way. Curtis Campher is late on the shot and is lucky to get an inside edge on that one. The ball goes past the leg stump and races away to the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Mohammad Amir to Curtis Campher, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Curtis Campher walks in with Ireland in a spot of bother.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Catastrophic start from Ireland but a more than perfect start for Pakistan here. Mohammad Amir comes in from over the stumps and just shortens the length a bit, bowling it with the wobble seam and angling it away from middle and leg. Paul Stirling shuffles to the leg side and comes down to open up the off side but only manages to get an outside edge which is gobble up by Mohammad Rizwan behind the stumps.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Rizwan b Mohammad Amir
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Mohammad Amir to Paul Stirling, OUT! c Mohammad Rizwan b Mohammad Amir.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Good length again and around leg stump, Harry Tector gets across the stumps and looks to flick it away but misses. The ball rolls off the pads behind square leg and they get a leg bye. Half an appeal for LBW but nothing doing.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mohammad Amir to Harry Tector, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls this one a bit fuller and a bit wider of the off stump and gets it to angle away, Harry Tector gets across the off stump and makes a leave.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mohammad Amir to Harry Tector, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and around off stump, Paul Stirling presses forward and eases it to covers for a quick single and he gets off the mark right away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mohammad Amir to Paul Stirling, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mohammad Amir to share the new ball with Shaheen Afridi.

Excellent onfield decision! Shaheen Afridi steams in and pitches the ball up again around off stump and forces the batter to play at it. Harry Tector looks to drive but seems to have been beaten past the inside edge. The ball takes a bit of pad and goes to the keeper. There is a huge appeal for LBW but it is turned down. Shaheen Afridi is certain that this is out and eventually, Babar Azam takes the review. Nothing on UltraEdge and Ball Tracking shows the wickets as missing. NOT OUT!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Harry Tector, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Harry Tector is the new man in.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! A double whammy for Shaheen Afridi inside the first over and Ireland are 2 for 2 with only five balls played. Shaheen pitches this one right up on the off stump line and gets the ball to go on with the angle rather shape back in. Lorcan Tucker looks to drive on the up but gets a thick outside edge that goes straight into the gloves of Mohammad Rizwan behind the stumps.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Rizwan b Shaheen Afridi
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shaheen Afridi to Lorcan Tucker, OUT! c Mohammad Rizwan b Shaheen Afridi.

Commentary.Commentary: Streaky first up from Lorcan Tucker but he is off the mark and so are Ireland. Just short of a good length and around off stump, Tucker walks down the track to avoid the movement and gets an inside edge past the stumps down to fine leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shaheen Afridi to Lorcan Tucker, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Lorcan Tucker walks in a number 3.

OUT! TIMBER! Shaheen Afridi with a wicket in the first over and Andy Balbirnie departs for a duck. Shaheen bowls this one on a good length around off and middle stump, Balbirnie looks to drive it through covers but it isn't full and the ball just slides back on after pitching. Balbirnie is beaten through the gate and the ball smashes into the stumps. Shaheen is delighted and rightfully so.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shaheen Afridi to Andy Balbirnie, OUT! b Shaheen Afridi.

Commentary.Commentary: A half-hearted shout for LBW but probably missing leg stump. A tad full and on middle and leg, this one hits the deck and nips back in a bit. Andy Balbirnie looks to flick but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Andy Balbirnie, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full to begin with but no signs of any swing. This is pitched up right on the off stump, trying to shape it back in, Andy Balbirnie watchfully pushes it out towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shaheen Afridi to Andy Balbirnie, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to get the match underway! The two umpires are out in the middle and the players of Pakistan are seen taking their places on the field. It will be the usual duo of Andy Balbirnie and skipper Paul Stirling that will open the innings for Pakistan. Shaheen Afridi has been handed the new ball and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the game but first, the match officials walk out to the middle and they are followed by the two sets of players who will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Ireland first followed by that of Pakistan.

The Irish skipper, Paul Stirling says that they would have bowled first as well and now will look to put runs on the board. Adds that they did manage to beat Pakistan leading up to the World Cup and didn't go on to win the series but this is a World Cup game and the feeling is different. Informs that they have one change in the side as Ben White comes in for Craig Young.

Babar Azam, the captain of Pakistan says that they will bowl first as the pitch has been under covers for three days. He adds that as a professional you need to prepare for each game and look to win it. Ends by informing that unfortunately Naseem Shah is out and Abbas Afridi comes in to replace him.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Andy Balbirnie, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Gareth Delany, Mark Adair, Barry McCarthy, Joshua Little, Ben White (In for Craig Young).

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Saim Ayub, Babar Azam (C), Fakhar Zaman, Usman Khan, Shadab Khan, Imad Wasim, Shaheen Afridi, Abbas Afridi (In for Naseem Shah), Haris Rauf, Mohammad Amir.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of Pakistan. Babar Azam decides to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Ramiz Raja is pitchside. He starts by saying that there is no rain but the outfield is still wet. Waqar Younis joins him and says that it has been under covers and reckons that the groundstaff have done well to prepare the pitch and a few grassy spots on the pitch will also aid the pacers. They add that the pitch is a bit damp and soft which will make things tricky for the batters and the captain who will win the toss should look to bowl first.

Ireland on the other hand have been pretty sub-par with their overall play and the batting just hasn't clicked at all, especially their experienced opening pair of skipper Paul Stirling and former skipper Andy Balbirnie. They looked in fine form coming into the World Cup with a few wins on the trot and that included inflicting defeat upon Pakistan as well. The Irish will look to use those wins against Pakistan to find some motivation and put on a much better all-round display than they have thus far. But will they be able to do so? Or will Pakistan get the win and send Ireland back home without a single win to their name? We shall find out in due course. Toss and team news in a bit.

Pakistan had their fate sealed when the game between Ireland and USA was washed out and USA got the one point they needed to qualify alongside India from this group. Things could have been completely different for Pakistan and they have only themselves to blame for those two losses against USA and India early on. They did manage to beat Canada but the team seems to be lacking cohesiveness and the batting has been all over the place. Skipper, Babar Azam and his deputy Mohammad Rizwan have mustered up runs but have been guilty of being a bit too passive with their approach and will be itching to go out and put on a much better showing to round off their campaign.

Hello and welcome back to Lauderhill in Florida for Match number 36 of the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup where Pakistan will go up against Ireland in the final game in Group A. We have had three washouts in Florida so far but thankfully, the weather forecast for this game looks very good with almost no chance of rain. On the cricketing front though, these two sides have had an underwhelming campaign and are out of competition but both teams will be eager to finish the campaign on a high.
... MATCH DAY ...

The Super 8s of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 are just a stone's throw away, and the excitement is through the roof as some teams have punched their tickets to the next round. However, this tournament has been a real roller coaster ride, with some major upsets along the way. Powerhouse nations like New Zealand and Pakistan have been shown the door much earlier than expected, while underdogs like the co-hosts USA have defied all odds and advanced to the next level in their maiden outing, turning the cricketing world on its head. Match 36 is a mere formality as Pakistan locks horns with Ireland in Group A. Both teams have had a World Cup campaign to forget, being knocked out of contention early after dropping their first two games. With nothing but pride to play for, this dead rubber clash is just going through the motions for the dejected outfits. Although Pakistan is coming off a victory against Canada, their campaign went horribly off-track as they lost to the USA in the Super Over, a heartbreaking defeat that will sting them for a long, long time. They then faced a demoralizing loss against India where they failed to chase down a modest total that derailed their campaign. The batters failed to bring their A-game to the party, leaving the bowlers high and dry time and again. And true to form, their shoddy fielding came back to haunt them and prove their undoing yet again this year. While Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam raked in the runs, their sluggish strike rates were a thorn in their side that invited criticism time and again. The batting duo's inability to break free from their shackles and cut loose had a domino effect on the batters to follow. Fakhar Zaman and Usman Khan too had a disappointing campaign. It's fair to say that Pakistan's batting lineup is overly dependent on the Rizwan-Babar duo, carrying the weight of the batting. If this pair fails to break the shackles, the middle order struggles to find its footing. However, Pakistan has historically been a force to be reckoned with when it comes to their bowling attack. The spearheads like Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, and Mohammad Amir didn't disappoint, leading the charge and delivering the goods. Although Haris Rauf struggled to keep a lid on the run flow, overall, they were decent, and had they received some responsible support from the batters, things might've been different for them. Ireland's campaign was also a non-starter as they failed to get any momentum going, tripping at the first hurdle with losses against India and surprisingly against Canada. Much like their rivals, they seemed like a fish out of the water, struggling to come to terms with the difficult conditions and failing to adapt their game accordingly. Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie, both seniors would be eager to break the shackles and get amongst the runs after an arid spell. Lorcan Tucker, Harry Tector, and Curtis Campher have all been off-color lately, failing to find their mojo and get into the groove. The all-rounders George Dockrell and Gareth Delany did put up a gritty fight against Canada, but couldn't quite get Ireland over the line as the top order went haywire. The pacers, on the other hand, ensured the wickets column kept ticking. Craig Young and Barry McCarthy, in particular, have been the pick of the bowlers, leading from the front while Delany too has pulled their weight as an all-arounder. Will Ireland end their campaign with a win or will Pakistan dominate? Or will rain play a spoilsport as the probability of an uninterrupted play looks bleak at the moment at Lauderhill, Florida? With nothing to gain from here in this competition, both teams might provide an opportunity and test the bench strength as well. Which team do you think will dominate?
